candidate.statement: mpz_invert(denom, denom, curve->p);  // TODO check status
candidate.selection_reason: curve parameters and point coordinates -> mpz_invert without checking return value -> may cause undefined behavior or incorrect result if inverse does not exist
candidate.source_summary: denom = 2 * pointP->y mod curve->p, where pointP->y is a curve point coordinate from caller; curve->p is a large prime modulus (P-256) set at curve construction.
candidate.sink_summary: The inverse result is used to compute lambda = numer * denom^{-1} mod p, then lambda is used to compute pointR coordinates. If mpz_invert returns 0 (no inverse), denom is left undefined and subsequent mpz_mul uses undefined value, leading to undefined behavior and incorrect point doubling result.
candidate.guard_summary: No validation that pointP->y != 0 mod p; no check of mpz_invert return value; no handling of point at infinity. The curve modulus p is prime (P-256) in the provided usage, so the only non-invertible case is when denom ≡ 0 mod p, i.e., when pointP->y ≡ 0 mod p.
candidate.risk_pattern: Missing error check on modular inverse in elliptic curve point doubling formula can cause undefined behavior and incorrect cryptographic results when doubling a point with y-coordinate zero modulo the field prime.
candidate.context_summary: In pointDouble, denom = 2 * y mod p. If y ≡ 0 mod p, denom ≡ 0, modular inverse does not exist, mpz_invert returns 0 and leaves denom undefined. The function proceeds to use undefined denom in multiplication, corrupting lambda and output point.
unresolved_facts: Whether callers of pointDouble ensure pointP->y ≠ 0 mod p; whether point with y=0 is a valid curve point on P-256; whether there is any handling of point at infinity elsewhere in the codebase.

target_cwe.description: The product does not check the return value from a method or function, which can prevent it from detecting unexpected states and conditions.
remediation_steps: Follow secure coding practices and security guidelines

stage3_hypothesis.fit_reason: mpz_invert return value indicating inverse failure is ignored, leading to undefined behavior in cryptographic computation
